title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Stellenbosch and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: South Africa's Wine of Origin system, since 1973, has regions, districts and wards. Stellenbosch is a district; wards include Simonsberg-Stellenbosch, Jonkershoek Valley and Banghoek. A certification seal on the bottle guarantees origin, grape and vintage, each at least 85%. Estate wine must be grown and made on one property.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Stellenbosch Cabernet suits steak, lamb and game like springbok. Pinotage suits the braai, South African barbecue, especially boerewors sausage, and bobotie, a spiced Cape Malay mince dish. Chenin Blanc suits seafood, chicken and mild curries. Serve reds at 16 to 18 degrees.

steps.prompt: Which South African dish suits Pinotage?
steps.explanation: Smoky grilled sausage suits Pinotage's fruit and smoke.

steps.body: Bobotie, a spiced, baked minced meat dish with a custard topping, also suits off-dry Chenin Blanc.

steps.prompt: South Africa's Wine of Origin seal certifies origin, grape and vintage.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Wine of Origin labels show district and ward
Cabernet suits steak and game; Pinotage suits the braai
Chenin suits seafood and mild curries
